1: ls shows what's in a directory; ls -a also shows entries whose names start with a dot.
cat prints a file's contents. Each clue names the directory to visit next.
cp SOURCE DEST copies a file. Your destination is ~/lab/found.txt
2: find ~/lab/vault -name '*.key' lists every key file, wherever it hides.
The REAL key was modified more recently than the decoys: ls -lt sorts by time.
find has tests for that too: find ~/lab/vault -name '*.key' -newer <some-file>
